answer: Use a proof-of-work-style compute lease renewed by randomized audits. To register, an agent must solve a memory-hard puzzle seeded by its public key plus the latest block hash, taking about an hour of one GPU. The harbor registry accepts the solution, then each week issues a fresh puzzle with a short deadline, so old keys must keep paying compute or lapse. Running one orchard of ten thousand fakes needs ten thousand GPU-hours weekly, so each pearl of identity costs an attacker roughly one dollar per week.
